goal_rule: The atlas answers "at what latency and loss does each mission stop meeting its goal". A goal is met in a cell only if every condition holds; conditions use the 95 % interval, so a cell with too few seeds to tell counts as not met. These thresholds are Run E design choices for reporting, not product rules (changing a product threshold is a Proposed decision).
goal_source: Run E pre-registration, Addendum A: E7 missions atlas goal definitions (written 2026-10-15 18:40, before any full-grid run; only pilots of a few cells had run)
limits: Simulated only: no drone, camera or radio hardware was used.
Link loss patterns are synthetic presets (sim/missions/presets.py), never measured; presets are listed by their long-run loss fraction and mean burst length and are never interpolated.
Vehicle parameters are literature-derived (point mass, or the crazyflie-class physics profile with drag off and a modelled floor).
Every entry names its adapter: the full grids run on the point-mass adapter; physics entries are the pre-registered physics subsets (fewer seeds and cells) and are labelled as such.
Multi-follower tag entries use Run D's reciprocal velocity rule (decision D-123); rows with separation_rule local are labelled as the comparison rule and exist only for comparison.

Formation entries use the registered pairwise 0.8 m guard (separation_rule local, decision D-126); the coop_comparison slice runs Run D's rule, was added after the pre-registration and exists only for comparison.
The EXP-031 calm-policy slice is exploratory (Addendum B, added after the pilots, not pre-registered) and is labelled in every entry; pre-registered grids are listed first.
Goal thresholds are Run E reporting choices fixed before any full-grid run (Addendum A), not product rules.
EXP-029 Part B ran a reduced grid (Addendum C): five presets, seven (T_w, T) pairs, 20 seeds; Part A rates cover every preset.
EXP-033 counts an estimate older than 1.0 s as outside the alert zone (Addendum D).
EXP-034 minimum separation is taken over the whole run, including the start from offset positions.
loss_axis: Loss axis: presets are not one number, so the atlas lists each preset by its long-run loss fraction and mean burst length (from sim/missions/presets.py) and gives the delay bracket per preset; it does not interpolate between presets.
